algorithm.title: Diagnostic Algorithm for Male Androgen Deficiency Syndrome.

cell.label: Positive screen on the ADAM questionnaire.

Evaluate comorbidities and other medical conditions. Measure morning fasting total testosterone (TT); also measure free testosterone (FT) if indicated (see Table 3). Avoid measuring TT if the patient is acutely ill.
Testosterone replacement is not indicated. Explore other causes (mood, weight, sexual dysfunction, drugs).
Hypogonadism confirmed. Order LH and FSH to distinguish primary from secondary hypogonadism. Measure PSA and hematocrit. Perform a DRE. Rule out reversible causes of testicular failure.

Rule out contraindications: breast or prostate cancer, severe untreated BPH, prostate nodule, PSA >4 ng/mL, PSA >3 ng/mL without further urologic evaluation, hematocrit >52%, untreated severe OSA, uncontrolled heart failure, MI or stroke within the last 6 months, thrombophilia, or planning fertility in the near term. Treatment is not routinely recommended for men 65 years or older.

footnotes.footnote: ADAM, Androgen Deficiency in the Aging Male; DRE, digital rectal examination; FT, free testosterone; OSA, obstructive sleep apnea; PSA, prostate-specific antigen; TT, total testosterone.
